We need to propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: steps forward: 1) carboxylic acid to amide (coupling). 2) Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). 3) sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). So retrosynthetic steps reverse order: Starting from target, we break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride and an aniline (the aryl amine). Then break amide to give carboxylic acid and aniline (the amide part). Then break α,β-unsaturated acid to give aldehyde and malonic acid (or maybe the unsaturated acid came from Doebner). So we need to propose precursors: 1) target -> sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride) + aniline (the phenyl with methyl). The sulfonyl chloride is attached to second phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). So we need to identify that ring: It's a phenyl sulfonyl attached to the first phenyl via sulfonamide. So precursor: p-tolyl amine (the first phenyl with methyl and amine) and p-sulfonyl chloride phenyl bearing the unsaturated amide side chain.

Thus step1 retrosynthesis: target -> two fragments: (A) 4-methyl aniline (p-toluidine) (SMILES: Cc1ccc(N)cc1) and (B) aryl sulfonyl chloride with side chain: ClSO2-Ph-... Actually sulfonyl chloride attached to phenyl ring: ClSO2-Ph-... The side chain is /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N attached at para position of that phenyl. So precursor B SMILES: ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2

Now step2: break amide: The side chain is C(=O)N-aryl (aniline). So amide formed from carboxylic acid (α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So precursor: α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid: /C=C/C(=O)H attached to phenyl ring (same phenyl). So unsaturated acid SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2 with sulfonyl chloride attached? Wait the sulfonyl chloride is on same phenyl, but after step2 we still have sulfonyl chloride attached. So precursor after step2: ClSO2-Ph-CH=CH-COOH (para). So SMILES: ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2

And the other fragment: aniline c3ccccc3N (SMILES: c1ccccc1N)

Step3: break α,β-unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid via Doebner modification. The forward Doebner: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid. So retrosynthesis: unsaturated acid -> aldehyde (aryl aldehyde) + malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). The aldehyde is the phenyl ring with aldehyde at para position relative to sulfonyl chloride? Actually the unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl via double bond at para position. The aldehyde precursor would be the same phenyl with aldehyde at that position: ClSO2-Ph-CHO (para). So SMILES: ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2

And malonic acid SMILES: C(C(=O)O)C(=O)O (or O=C(O)C(=O)O). Use standard: O=C(O)C(=O)O

Thus we have 3 steps.

Now need to find template IDs for each transformation. We can search for templates matching these transformations.

Step1: sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide). Search criteria: functional_groups_formed: sulfonamides; functional_groups_broken: amine, sulfonyl chloride? Actually forward reaction forms sulfonamide, breaks S-Cl bond and N-H bond. So functional_groups_formed: sulfonamides; functional_groups_broken: sulfonyl chloride, primary amine. Let's search.
